director.chapterArc: A chapter of tactical recalibration following a night of revelation. The tone shifts from Toren's naive expectation of gentleness to Rook's brutal pragmatism, then moves through Dessa's quiet discovery of her Ember status and Ott's urgent intelligence about the enemy. It culminates in Rook sacrificing his own reserves for Senna and making an impossible choice that redefines their survival strategy.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, observational distance throughout. Do not dramatize Rook's cruelty or Dessa's power; let the facts carry the weight. The emotional peaks are internal (Rook's sacrifice) rather than external shouting matches.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal expectation of a softer morning; the narrator sets up the contrast with reality.
cues.from: Toren had spent a good part of the four hours he had actually slept preparing for a different day. He had worked out, lying on his back watching the sparks go, that things were going to be gentler now, and that there would be a period of some days in which everybody was careful with everybody, and that the man would be — he had not been able to finish the thought, but the word hanging about at the end of it had been warmer.
cues.through: What happened was that Rook got up at grey light, put the fire out, said "Up. Line. On the flat by the gate," and ran them for fifty minutes, and it was the worst fifty minutes in a fortnight.
cues.reason: Establishes Toren's naive hope before Rook's drill begins.

cues.delivery: Rook's dialogue delivered with flat, unyielding authority; no rising inflection on questions or commands.
cues.from: He took Toren's footwork apart twice. He made Milo do the light-on-the-ground thing eleven times, until Milo could set it down and step off it without looking. He told Wyck that his left hand was a liability and that he had four months to make it a merely poor hand and that he was going to be unpleasant about it every single morning until then, and Wyck said "Right," and did it again.
cues.through: "After all that," Rook agreed, "there are still four of you on a road with a cart, and this country is worse than the country behind, and nothing I said at that fire puts one thing between any of you and what's out here." He slung his coat. "Knowing a thing and doing it while frightened are two separate skills. That hasn't stopped being true because I've had a bad night."
cues.reason: Character voice: Rook is economical and stoic. The drill description must feel clinical.

cues.delivery: Dessa's voice is analytical and calm; she speaks with quiet intensity rather than anger.
cues.through: "He's exactly the same, and it's completely different," said Dessa. "Milo. He's not going to start being nice. He was never going to start being nice, and if he had, I'd be frightened. The difference isn't in him, it's that when he says something horrible now, we know where it comes from." She got herself up off the gate. "He'll be reserved and difficult for the rest of his life. That's fine. I'd just rather be difficult with somebody than at them."
cues.reason: Character voice: Dessa uses logic to process emotion. Her observation of Rook must sound like a deduction.

cues.delivery: Narrative focus on the stillness and sensory detail of Dessa's state; a shift from action to observation.
cues.from: Toren was at the tailgate with his grandmother and heard Dessa say, from six feet away in the grass, in a voice with nothing in it at all:
cues.through: She was sitting in the grass with her bad leg out and her hands open on her knees, exactly as she had sat on nineteen banks in twenty-eight days, and she had her eyes open, and she was looking at nothing, and her face had gone the way it had gone at the field wall — the face of somebody who has said a word in a language she does not speak and been understood.
cues.reason: Scene turn: The discovery moment requires silence and clarity.

cues.delivery: Dessa's dialogue delivered with precise, rapid-fire accuracy; Rook's responses are brief and confirming.
cues.from: "Milo's behind the cart," said Dessa. "He's at the off-side wheel and he's crouched down doing the strap and he's got the mug in his other hand. Wyck's at eleven paces, straight up the slope, standing still. The mule's — the mule's further than I thought, the mule's at about twenty-six and it's eating. Senna's in the cart and she's sat up. Tor's at the tailgate and he's turned round now, he's turned round because I said your name."
cues.reason: Character voice: Dessa is reporting facts. The rhythm should be clipped but not frantic.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation of the 'Reading' is delivered as a technical briefing; dry and instructional.
cues.from: "Now," said Rook. "Last night I gave you a word and said I'd come back to it. This is it. This is a Reading, and this is what it is: you sit still, and you take honest stock of what's in you, from the inside, and you say it as a fraction, out loud, in a number a person can use.
cues.through: "And it isn't going down because it's lit, not spent. That's the whole difference, and it's the one everybody has to be shown twice." He sat back on his heels. "Dessa Cole. That's Ember. That's the rank, and that's the word people will use about you now, and they'll be right, and I'd like you to hear the rest of it before anybody says anything else.
cues.reason: Character voice: Rook treats magic mechanics like logistics. No wonder tones.

cues.delivery: Rook's definition of 'Ember' is delivered with weight and finality; the contrast between Kindled and Ember must be clear.
cues.from: "Kindled is a door standing open. Ember is the first thing that stays lit when you stop looking at it. He got there on a towpath with a sack of corn on his chest" — a nod at Toren — "and that one got there on a press-house step without noticing he'd done it, and you have got there sitting in wet grass on nineteen separate evenings getting nothing, which is the hardest of the three by a distance, and the other two should think about that."
cues.through: "A man who can put a shape on the end of his arm is worth having. A person who knows where all six of you are in the dark, all the time, without looking, is worth the whole of the rest of the party, and everybody finds that out at about four in the morning on the worst night of their lives."
cues.reason: Key revelation: The distinction in power levels needs to land without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Dessa's explanation of her realization is delivered with a sense of relief and clarity; the firelight setting should feel intimate.
cues.from: "Because I stopped trying to prove it was mine," she said.
cues.through: "You can't reach it while you're still asking whether you're allowed to."
cues.reason: Character voice: Dessa has found acceptance. Her tone shifts from questioning to stating.

cues.delivery: Ott's arrival is brisk and professional; her news must be delivered with a sense of urgency but without panic.
cues.from: They met Ott on the thirtieth day, four miles short of a crossroads, coming the other way.
cues.reason: Scene turn: The shift from camp routine to external threat requires a change in pacing.

cues.delivery: The exchange of the brass chit is handled with ritualistic slowness; Rook's reaction to 'Tull' must be subtle but palpable.
cues.from: Rook took the piece of brass out of his coat.
cues.reason: Key revelation: The name drop requires a pause for impact.

cues.delivery: Rook's arithmetic is delivered with cold precision; the stakes are high but his voice remains steady.
cues.from: Toren did the arithmetic in his head before anybody said anything, and got it wrong twice, and then got it, and wished he hadn't.
cues.through: "That's two days out. Then whatever happens at the other end takes as long as it takes, and I'd give it a day, and then it's three days back at a walk if I come back the same way, and I might not be able to come back the same way. Call it six days minimum and eight if it goes poorly, and it will go poorly, because it's forty men in a walled yard, and I'm one."
cues.reason: Character voice: Rook calculates survival. The numbers must feel heavy.

cues.delivery: Rook's refusal is delivered with absolute finality; the shift from negotiation to decision must be sharp.
cues.from: "And here's the other column, and I'd like everybody to watch me do it, because this is the bit I'd usually keep.
cues.through: "I'm not doing it." He picked his coat up off the cart shaft. "And I want one thing understood, because Milo's face is doing something, and I'd rather kill it now. I'm not being noble. There isn't a noble version of this. What I am doing is choosing which of two things I want more, and I've chosen, and I'm going to be poor company about it for a while."
cues.reason: Scene turn: Rook rejects Senna's suggestion. This requires a clear vocal boundary.

cues.delivery: Rook pouring the ash is delivered with quiet gravity; his explanation of his own diminished state must sound matter-of-fact.
cues.from: Then he drank about half of what was in it, and poured the rest into Senna's cup, which is a thing Toren had never seen anybody do in his life and had not known was possible.
cues.through: "You've had a month. This is the week you find out what it was for."
cues.reason: Key revelation: The sacrifice requires a pause for emotional weight.

cues.delivery: The final conversation between Rook and Toren is delivered with a sense of shared burden; the silence should feel heavy.
cues.from: Toren went up the bank at about the fourth hour because he could not sleep and because he had known for six hours that he was going to.
cues.through: "And I'd do it the same way tomorrow," he said, "and that's the part I can't get to sit down flat."
cues.reason: Scene turn: The quiet resolution requires restraint.

pauses.reason: Completed thought; Toren's expectation vs. reality contrast.

pauses.after: "I can't see any of them," said Dessa. "I've got my back to the whole camp and I have not turned round once and I can't see a single one of them and I know exactly where they all are."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; the revelation of her power needs space to land.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the impossibility of her claim; a reversal of expectation.

pauses.before: Now stop talking about it for a minute
pauses.reason: Emphasis on Rook's command to shift focus; the pivot point of the scene.
Completed thought; confirmation of ability achieved.

Speaker reset; Ott's news changes the scene dynamic.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the location of the threat; a critical plot point.

pauses.after: "Tull's sixth is what's at Barrow Gate," said Ott. "That's the name on the table. That's the name the man with the box says forty times a day."
pauses.reason: Completed thought; 'Tull' is a specific threat name that needs emphasis.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the specific enemy unit; a name that carries history.

pauses.after: "It's that six days is the number if I come back."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; the core of Rook's decision ('if I come back') must resonate.

pauses.before: It's that six days is the number if I come back
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the condition of Rook's decision; the crux of his sacrifice.

pauses.after: "It's ash out of a road seam, and there's nine days of me in that flask, and I've just spent the lot," said Rook. "It buys her about four days of walking she wouldn't otherwise have, and it is the best use anything in my possession has ever been put to."
pauses.reason: Completed thought; the sacrifice is stated clearly.

pauses.before: It buys her about four days
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the specific value of Rook's sacrifice; a tangible cost.

pauses.before: Four, by the time we've done two more
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the dwindling timeline; a countdown that adds tension.

pauses.before: And I'd do it the same way tomorrow
pauses.reason: Emphasis on Rook's resolve; a statement of character integrity.

pauses.after: "Go to sleep," he said, at last — and it was the same two words he had used on a bridge and at a field wall and on a gravel bar at midnight, and this time he moved over about a foot to make room on the bank, and did not say anything about having done it.
pauses.reason: Scene break/end of chapter; final image requires a long rest to let the mood settle.
